title: The Thorn of the Sundered Sea
premise: Tamsin Reyes has spent twelve years hiding her hedge-witch training in Saltmere, a city that outlawed magic after the Sundering split its harbor from the sea. When she discovers tonight's date circled in a century-old prophecy book she bought for the paper, she is dragged into the prophecy's fulfillment: the winter that never ends is the work of the Hollow King, a dead monarch whose crown is worn and animated by the thorn-thing that killed him. Guided by the prophecy's reluctant other subject — a disgraced royal cartographer named Edric Vale — Tamsin learns the thorn can only be unbound by someone who carries the old blood of the hedge-witches who first crowned the king. The price of that unbinding is her own name and magic, surrendered to the thorn in the king's place. In the end Tamsin pays it, the Hollow King dies human and free, the winter breaks, and Tamsin — nameless but alive, and quietly beginning again — chooses who she will be without the inheritance she never wanted.
about_author: Rosalind Iversen is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing salvaged ship logs and harbor charts before turning to fantasy. She writes about stubborn women, haunted coastlines, and the paperwork of old magic.

chapters.title: Charms for the Lawful
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She sells a luck-knot to a dockworker in magic-outlawed Saltmere, hiding her craft behind harmless trinkets. Establishes her survival rules and her loneliness. Beat: cautious contentment built on a lie.

chapters.title: The Book That Knew the Date
chapters.summary: Tamsin buys a water-damaged prophecy book for its blank pages and finds today's date circled a century ago, with her own description beneath. Beat: dread cracking open the ordinary.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Debt
chapters.summary: Edric Vale's POV. A disgraced royal cartographer recognizes the prophecy's second figure — himself — and comes hunting the girl who matches it. Beat: guilt sharpened into purpose.

chapters.title: Taken by the Page
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. At moonrise the prophecy activates; the page pulls her through into the frozen ruins of the old capital. She wakes in snow beside Edric. Beat: terror and unwilling alliance.

chapters.title: What the Sundering Broke
chapters.summary: Edric's POV. He explains the Sundering: the harbor torn away, magic outlawed, the king dead and crowned by something else. Tamsin refuses the quest. Beat: bitter history versus denial.

chapters.title: The First Long Night
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Surviving a blight-storm in a waystation, Tamsin uses forbidden magic to save them both and sees Edric's fear of her. Beat: shame and the cost of being seen.

chapters.title: Hedge-Blood
chapters.summary: Edric's POV. In an abandoned chapel he finds records showing the hedge-witches made the crown — and Tamsin's lineage is the key. He hides this from her. Beat: the first betrayal seeded.

chapters.title: The Village That Waited
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A snowbound village worships the Hollow King as a saint; Tamsin witnesses what the endless winter does to ordinary hope. Beat: compassion hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Thorn Wears the Crown
chapters.summary: Edric's POV. They reach the palace outskirts and see the Hollow King walking the walls — alive, dead, and wrong. The thorn senses Tamsin's blood and marks her. Beat: horror made intimate.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Running
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Trapped in a cellar, Tamsin finally tells Edric why she fled her mistress: she was to be the hedge-coven's next sacrifice to the crown. Beat: vulnerability exchanged for trust.

chapters.title: The Map of the Under-Harbor
chapters.summary: Edric's POV. Edric confesses he helped draw the wards that outlawed magic; his redemption arc begins as he maps a drowned route into the palace. Beat: guilt turned to purpose.

chapters.title: Drowned Streets
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. They cross the sunken harbor through frozen water and sunken ships, nearly drowning when the thorn's roots find them. Beat: partnership forged under pressure.

chapters.title: The Court of Salt and Ice
chapters.summary: Edric's POV. Inside the palace they find the old court, preserved mid-flight, and the prophecy's final page — which names the price: a life freely given. Beat: dread with the stakes made explicit.

chapters.title: What Edric Did Not Say
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin finds Edric's hidden notes proving he knew her blood was the price from the start. She confronts him; the alliance shatters. Beat: betrayal and heartbreak.

chapters.title: Alone in the Long Winter
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin goes on alone through the thorn-tangled palace, using every trick of her hedge-craft, and nearly dies at the throne room door. Beat: rock bottom, self-reliance tested.

chapters.title: The King Beneath
chapters.summary: Edric's POV. Edric, following in penance, finds the true king's body beneath the throne — still breathing, twelve years of winter leaking from his wounds. Beat: pity replacing fear.

chapters.title: The Hollow Court
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin faces the Hollow King; the thorn offers her a bargain — serve it, and live. She sees in it her old mistress's logic: survival at any price. Beat: temptation and refusal.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, climax. With Edric holding the wards open, Tamsin begins the unbinding, giving her name and magic to the thorn. The king dies human; the thorn takes her gift instead of her life. Beat: sacrifice at the peak.

chapters.title: The Breaking of Winter
chapters.summary: Edric's POV. The thorn dies with Tamsin's magic in its roots; the Sundered Sea roars back into the harbor as the ice fails. Edric carries the nameless Tamsin out of the falling palace. Beat: catharsis and release.

chapters.title: A City Without Laws on Magic
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Saltmere thaws; the outlawry collapses with the winter. Tamsin, stripped of power, watches others reclaim open magic she no longer has. Beat: grief for the lost inheritance.

chapters.title: The Name She Chooses
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Offered restoration by the hedge-witches' survivors — at the same price her mistress once demanded — Tamsin refuses. She keeps her empty hands. Beat: identity chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: Charms for the Lawful, Again
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, resolution. Spring in Saltmere: Tamsin sells honest trinkets beside Edric's restored maps, teaching hedge-craft as ordinary knowledge, no sacrifice required. Beat: quiet, earned peace.
